name: q2_late_hover_gps_observability_v1
question: Do the 26 input channels (and their combinations) contain information that separates late-hover GPS fault windows from late-hover normal windows? Is the late-hover GPS bottleneck a model-capability problem or an input-information limit?
why_new: 11-05 hover_separability measured only per-channel mean/std and a 130-d GBT on val (8-10 GPS cases, AUC 0.80), without fault-mode stratification, cross-channel physics features, flight-identity control or raw-GPS reference. RflyMAD GPS faults are mode 4 (multiplicative scale 0.9/1.0/1.1 on three axes, 27 combinations incl. identity) or mode 3 (noise); this split was never used.
training: CPU probes only (HistGradientBoosting); no neural network training
data_boundary: train split only. No val, internal test or Real. Raw RflyMAD vehicle_gps_position used only as an outside-input reference (Part B).

population.positive: train late-hover GPS fault windows (942 windows, 40 cases: mode 3 4 cases/144 windows; mode 4 36 cases/798 windows, of which z-factor = 1: 313 windows; identity (1,1,1): 2 cases/46 windows)
population.negative: train late-hover independent normal windows (1237 windows, 55 cases)

features.F0: existing 130-d window statistics (mean, std, min, max, mean |diff| per channel)
features.F1: F0 + per channel q10, q50, q90, linear slope, last-first, FFT band energy 0-1/1-3/3-8/8-25 Hz
features.F2: F1 + cross-channel physics consistency: NED accel from quaternion-rotated accel minus g vs d(vel)/dt (per-axis residual mean/std/max abs, window delta-v vs integrated accel), baro rate vs -vel_z (residual mean/std, delta baro vs -integrated vel_z), horizontal speed mean/max, tilt mean/std

part_A_26ch.channel_groups: actuator_ctrl(4), actuator_out(4), gyro(3), accel(3)+acc_norm, baro(1), attitude(4), velocity(3), mag(3), physics(cross-channel); group-only probes on F1 features of that group
part_A_26ch.probe: HistGradientBoostingClassifier(max_iter 400, lr 0.05, max_leaf_nodes 31, l2 1.0, random_state 0), balanced class weights, 3-fold group CV with folds sha256('h1cv|'+association_group)%3, out-of-fold probabilities
part_A_26ch.existing_models: global T0, T1 (seed-mean AUC over 42-46), GBT, E1 scores restricted to the same windows
part_A_26ch.confound_control: same F2 probe separating GPS-hover pre-fault windows from independent-normal hover windows with matched window end time 10-21.7 s (both normal); measures flight-identity leakage
part_A_26ch.metrics: AUC per stratum with association_group cluster bootstrap 95% CI (2000, rng 20261106); recall at 5% and 10% late-hover normal FPR; paired AUC difference probe minus best existing model

part_B_raw_gps.purpose: outside-26ch reference: does the fault exist in the raw GPS sensor at all during late hover
part_B_raw_gps.features_per_case: GPS relative altitude / baro relative altitude ratio in late hover (relative to takeoff), GPS horizontal position std and drift in late hover
part_B_raw_gps.comparison: late-hover GPS fault cases by stratum vs the 55 train independent-normal hover flights; case-level AUC

decision_rule.info_present: best Part-A probe AUC >= 0.90 with CI lower >= 0.85, and confound-control AUC <= 0.70
decision_rule.not_observable_26ch: best Part-A probe AUC CI upper < 0.75
decision_rule.model_capability_gap: info_present and probe minus best existing model AUC with CI lower > 0.05
decision_rule.input_limit: not_observable_26ch in a stratum and Part B separates that stratum (case AUC >= 0.90)
decision_rule.physical_or_label_limit: not observable in Part A and not separated in Part B for that stratum (fault leaves no measurable effect in hover)

expected_information_gain: Whether the late-hover GPS recall requirement is achievable from current inputs; which GPS fault modes are detectable; whether to treat late-hover GPS as a model problem, an input-contract problem, or a label/physics limitation when fixing the source-model operating point.
not_allowed: changing strata or thresholds after results
